# Volume 5 — CHAPTER XXVI. MISS WINIFRED GETS A NEW POINT OF VIEW

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Tabitha, once my life is over, my return to earth will happen whenever the daffodils bloom in this garden,” Nell remarked with great joy. “I might be invisible to everyone, yet this is where I will be. Should someone happen to be in the garden then—my arrival will likely occur on an evening identical to this one, though a gorgeous, pale-pinkish spring dawn is also a possibility—the daffodils will simply be seen swaying vigorously by them as though swept by a stronger burst of wind, but it will actually be me.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0000 }

“In truth, dear Mrs. Dr., after your passing, you won’t consider showing off secular items such as daffies,” Tabitha remarked. “Furthermore, ghosts, whether visible or invisible, are not something I believe in.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0001 }

“Oh, Tabitha, I will not become a ghost! The word sounds so dreadful. I will merely remain myself. Whether it be morning or evening, I will scamper about in the twilight and visit every place dear to me. Tabitha, do you recall how deeply grieved I was upon departing from our tiny House of Dreams? I believed I could never cherish Hollowmere to the same degree. Yet I do. Every single inch of this land, along with every stick and stone upon it, is precious to me.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0002 }

“The location pleases me quite a bit,” stated Tabitha, whose life would have ended had she ever been taken away from it, “yet our hearts ought not to be excessively tied to worldly possessions, my dear Mrs. Dr. Disasters like fires and earthquakes do occur. Being ready at all times is our duty. Three nights back, the home of the Tom MacAllisters across the harbour was destroyed by fire. It is claimed by some that Tom MacAllister started the blaze on his own home to collect the insurance money. Whether that is true or false, I cannot say. Even so, my recommendation is that the doctor inspect our chimneys immediately. Preventing trouble takes far less effort than fixing it later. Look there, Mrs. Ambrose Kerr is walking through the gate, wearing an expression that suggests she was summoned but found herself unable to attend.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0003 }

“Has the Journal crossed your path today, my sweet Nell?”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0004 }

Miss Winifred had a tremble in her voice, caused in part by her feelings, and in part because she had rushed up from the store so quickly that she had run out of breath.
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0005 }

Nell leaned above the daffodils so that her smile would be concealed. That day, she and Hugh had chuckled loudly and unfeelingly about the front page of the Journal, yet she was aware that dear Miss Winifred regarded it as nearly a tragedy, so she had to avoid hurting her feelings through any show of lightheartedness.
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0006 }

“Is it not terrible? What can we do?” inquired Miss Winifred in despair. Although Miss Winifred had declared that she would no longer fret about the tricks of the children at the manse, she continued to fret all the same.
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0007 }

Going first, Nell headed for the veranda, a spot where Tabitha sat engaged in her knitting, flanked by Harcourt and Tessa who were both studying their primers. At this point, Tabitha had already started working on a second pair of stockings intended for Grace. Worry over poor humanity was something Tabitha never experienced. Whatever she could manage for its improvement she accomplished, before peacefully entrusting everything else to the Higher Powers.
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0008 }

“Winifred Kerr believes this world was created for her to manage, Mrs. Dr. dear,” she had remarked to Nell on one occasion, “which keeps her constantly agitated about one thing or another. I have never held that view about myself, allowing me to proceed peacefully. Though it has occasionally crossed my mind that affairs could perhaps be administered somewhat more efficiently than their current state. Still, it is improper for us miserable worms to entertain these ideas. Such notions merely cause us distress without achieving anything.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0009 }

“Now, I fail to see how any action can be taken,” remarked Nell, as she drew a comfortable, plush seat forward for Miss Winifred. “Yet in what possible way did Mr. Vickers permit the publication of that letter? He certainly ought to have possessed greater judgment.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0010 }

“Well, he is gone, Nell dearie—for a week now he has been away in New Brunswick. In his absence, that young scalawag Joe Vickers is editing the Journal. Mr. Vickers himself would certainly never have printed it, even though he is a Methodist, but Joe would merely consider it a fine joke. Just as you say, I do not imagine there is anything that can be done at this point, except live it down. However, if I ever catch Joe Vickers trapped in a corner somewhere, I will deliver a talking to that he will not quickly forget. I wished Ambrose to cancel our subscription to the Journal right away, but he did nothing but laugh and remark that the edition today was the single one containing anything readable for a year. Ambrose will not ever treat anything seriously—just like a man. As luck would have it, Evan Garrick resembles him in that way. He regards it as a joke and is laughing everywhere about it. Yet he is another Methodist! Regarding Mrs. Burr of Upper Glen, she will naturally be enraged and they will quit the church. Not that losing them will be a significant loss in any way. The Methodists are entirely welcome to have them.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0011 }

“Mrs. Burr gets what she deserves,” remarked Tabitha, who harbored a long-standing grudge against that particular woman and had been greatly amused by the mention of her in the letter from Grace. “She is going to realize that she cannot swindle the Methodist minister out of his pay using inferior yarn.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0012 }

“The worst part about it is that there is little chance of conditions improving,” Miss Winifred remarked despondently. “While Mr. Ashdown was still visiting Clementine Ainslie, I harbored a real hope that a proper mistress would shortly be at the manse. However, that has completely ended. It is my guess she refused him because of the children—or rather, that appears to be what everyone believes.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0013 }

“It is my belief that he never made a proposal to her,” remarked Tabitha, as she was unable to imagine a person declining a minister.
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0014 }

“Indeed, that remains a complete mystery to everyone. However, it is beyond doubt that his visits there have ceased. Furthermore, Clementine appeared unwell throughout the spring season. It is my hope that her time in Portmaris proves beneficial for her. She departed one month ago and, as I gather, intends to remain for one more month. I am unable to recall a previous occasion when Clementine was absent from home. She and Harriet were always completely inseparable. Nevertheless, my understanding is that Harriet demanded she take this trip. In the meantime, Harriet and Lionel Fairlie are reheating the old soup.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0015 }

“Does that actually hold true?” inquired Nell, with a chuckle. “Word of it reached my ears, yet it seemed scarcely believable to me.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0016 }

“Accept it as true! You can certainly take it as fact, Nell, my dear. No one lacks knowledge of this. Lionel Fairlie did not ever leave a single person uncertain about what he intended regarding any issue. The courting he engaged in was always done openly in front of everyone. He mentioned to Ambrose that Harriet hadn't entered his thoughts for years, yet during his initial visit to church last autumn, he caught sight of her and succumbed to love for her once more. He remarked that he had completely forgotten her great beauty. Two decades had passed since he last beheld her, if that seems credible to you. Naturally, he abstained from attending church services, whereas Harriet frequented no other places in these parts. Ah, every one of us understands Lionel's intentions, but the intentions of Harriet are an entirely separate issue. I will not assume the responsibility of forecasting if a wedding will result or not.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0017 }

“It appears that being jilted by him once does not matter to certain individuals, Mrs. Dr. dear,” Tabitha observed in a somewhat bitter tone.
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0018 }

“He abandoned her during an angry outburst and regretted it for the rest of his days,” Miss Winifred remarked. “That is not like a calculating abandonment. As for me, Lionel was never an object of my hatred like he was for others. He was incapable of intimidating me. I really am curious about what prompted him to begin attending church. Mrs. Wilsons’s claim that Grace Ashdown visited him and intimidated him into going is something I could never credit. Asking Grace directly has always been my intention, yet the thought never crossed my mind on the occasions I met her. How could Grace Ashdown possibly sway Lionel Fairlie? When I departed, he was still inside the store, roaring with amusement about that disgraceful letter. His voice was loud enough to reach Seven Gulls Point. ‘The greatest girl in the world,’ he was yelling. ‘She’s so packed with spirit that it’s overflowing. And every single old biddy wants to subdue her, blast them. However, they will never manage it—never! It would be like attempting to submerge a fish. Garrick, ensure you apply additional fertilizer to your potato crop next season. Ho, ho, ho!’ Whereupon his laughter rattled the very roof.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0019 }

“Tabitha observed, “At any rate, the compensation Mr. Fairlie offers is generous.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0020 }

“Well, in certain respects Lionel lacks malice. A thousand would be handed over by him without fluttering an eyelid, yet he would bellow like a Bashan Bull should an overcharge of merely five cents be demanded of him. On top of that, Mr. Ashdown’s preaching pleases him, and Lionel Fairlie remained consistently ready to fork over money provided his intellect received a stimulating jolt. About him there exists no greater amount of Christianity than can be found in a dark, unclothed pagan within Africa, nor shall there ever be. Nevertheless, possessing intelligence and extensive reading, he evaluates sermons in the same manner he would speeches. In any case, his support for Mr. Ashdown and the young ones comes at a good time, since after these events their necessity for allies will be greater than before. Trust me, offering justifications on their behalf has exhausted me.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0021 }

“I wonder, dear Miss Winifred,” Nell remarked gravely, “if we have not all been fashioning far too many excuses. We are being extremely silly, and it is time for us to cease. Let me inform you of what I should love to do. Naturally, I shall refrain from doing it”—Nell had observed a flash of apprehension in Tabitha’s eye—“it would stray too far from convention, and once we attain what is deemed a dignified age, we are obliged to remain conventional or perish. Even so, I should love to do it. I should love to convene a gathering of the Ladies Aid, the W.M.S., and the Girls Sewing Society, while admitting into the audience every single Methodist who has been finding fault with the Ashdowns—though I truly believe that if we Presbyterians ceased our finding fault and excusing, we would discover that alternative denominations would bother themselves scarcely at all regarding the people in our manse. I would address them, ‘Dear Christian friends’—stressing ‘Christian’ with clear intent—‘I possess a message for you and I desire to deliver it firmly and forcefully, so that you may carry it back and reiterate it to your households. You Methodists have no occasion to feel sorry for us, nor do we Presbyterians need to feel sorry for ourselves. We intend to stop doing so immediately. Furthermore, we are going to declare, with courage and honesty, to every critic and sympathizer, “We take pride in our minister and his household. Mr. Ashdown stands as the finest preacher Glen St. Agnes church has ever possessed. In addition, he serves as a genuine, devoted instructor of truth and Christian charity. He proves to be a loyal friend, a wise pastor in every vital aspect, and a polished, learned, well-mannered gentleman. His household is deserving of him. Gerald Ashdown ranks as the brightest student in the Glen school, and Mr. Hazard asserts that he is bound for a splendid future. He represents a courageous, principled, truthful young boy. Grace Ashdown is a striking beauty, and she is just as uplifting and creative as she is gorgeous. There is not a single ordinary thing about her. The entirety of the remaining girls in the Glen combined do not possess the spirit, cleverness, cheerfulness, and ‘spunk’ that belong to her. She does not have a single adversary anywhere. Each person acquainted with her adores her. Regarding how many individuals, whether young ones or adults, can such a statement be made? Ida Ashdown embodies pure gentleness. She is bound to develop into an exceedingly endearing woman. Rupert Ashdown, owing to his fondness for ants, frogs, and spiders, will eventually become a naturalist whom the whole of Canada—indeed, the whole world—will take joy in honoring. Are you aware of any alternative family inside the Glen, or beyond it, regarding whom every one of these statements can be uttered? Banish all sheepish excuses and apologies. We exult in our minister along with his marvelous sons and daughters!”’
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0022 }

Nell came to a halt, influenced in part by the breathlessness that followed her impassioned utterance, and in part because the expression on Miss Winifred’s face warned her against risking any more words. The kindly woman was gazing powerlessly at Nell, seemingly overwhelmed by a sea of unfamiliar thoughts. Nevertheless, she surfaced with a gasp and bravely made her way toward land.
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0023 }

“Nell Carrow, my wish is that you would convene that gathering and state precisely those words! As one individual, you have caused me to feel embarrassment for my actions, and I certainly will not decline to acknowledge it. Undoubtedly, that represents the manner in which we ought to have spoken—most of all to the Methodists. Furthermore, every single word of it is the truth—all of it. We have simply been closing our vision to the important, valuable matters and narrowing it upon the trivial details that are not worth a pin. Oh, dearie Nell, I am capable of recognizing a point once it has been driven into my mind. I will offer no further apologies for Winifred Ambrose! Following this, I am going to keep my head held high, you can be sure—even if I might still discuss matters with you as I normally do merely to vent my emotions in the event that the Ashdowns perform further shocking actions. Even regarding that letter that made me feel so terrible—well, it is nothing more than a fine jest when all is said, just as Lionel states. Few young women would possess the cleverness to conceive of composing it—with all the punctuation so well executed and without a single word spelled incorrectly. Simply permit me to listen to any Methodist utter a single comment concerning it—even if, despite everything, I am never going to pardon Joe Vickers—you may trust me! To-night, where are the remaining members of your young brood?”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0024 }

“Fern Hollow is where Edmund and the twins are. As for Kit, the garret is where she is studying.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0025 }

“Fern Hollow has them all completely infatuated. Mary Stubbs considers it the sole place worth being in the universe. Were I to allow it, she would spend every single night up here. However, I refrain from fostering her roaming habits. Furthermore, Nell dearie, her absence leaves a void for me. I never anticipated developing such deep affection for her. That is not to say I am blind to her flaws and fail to amend them. Nevertheless, from the moment she entered my dwelling, not a single impudent word has passed her lips toward me, and her assistance is immense—because when everything is taken into account, Nell dearie, my youth has slipped away, and refusing to acknowledge it is useless. Fifty-nine was my age on my previous birthday. I fail to feel that old, yet disputing the Family Bible is impossible.”
{: #nw-v05-c26-p0026 }
